findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced KMS/SSE default. Sensitive report data is left unencrypted by configuration.

No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy accompanies this bucket, leaving it reliant on account defaults and vulnerable to accidental public ACL/policy grants.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this bucket containing vendor data is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.
There is no bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial ledger data is stored without an enforced encryption default.
Although the ACL is private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, so a future policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly without any account-level guardrail.
No logging block is configured for this ledger bucket, leaving no audit trail of object access for sensitive financial exports.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, allowing cleartext HTTP access to ledger export objects.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so public ACLs or policies could be applied without being blocked.

The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures, and credential-handling detail and are stored unencrypted by default here.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against inadvertent public ACL or policy grants.
The audit log destination bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so log data integrity and confidentiality depend solely on account defaults.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket combined with no object lock / MFA delete means audit evidence can be irreversibly destroyed by a single Terraform apply, undermining log integrity.
The object is uploaded to the unencrypted reports_archive bucket with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument, so this vendor roster file is stored in cleartext at rest.
